%% @spec walkthrough/2
%% @title Sign in with OAuth (PKCE)
%% @trigger The user clicks "Sign in with Acme" on a page that has no session cookie yet.
%% @term PKCE: Proof Key for Code Exchange; the app makes a random secret, sends only its hash first, and proves it owns the secret later, so a stolen code is useless.
%% @term authorization code: a short-lived one-time code the identity provider hands to the browser, which the backend swaps for tokens.
%% @term refresh token: a long-lived token used to get a new access token quietly when the old one expires; it is kept on the server, never in the browser.
%% @term HttpOnly cookie: a cookie that page scripts cannot read, so a cross-site-scripting bug cannot steal it.
%% @layer U kind=person The person signing in.
%% @layer APP kind=client Single-page web app. Starts the login and never sees a password or a refresh token.
%% @layer API kind=service Our backend. Swaps the one-time code for tokens and keeps them in a server-side session.
%% @layer IDP kind=external Identity provider (OAuth 2.1 / OpenID Connect). Checks the password and MFA, then issues the tokens.
%% @layer DB kind=db Session store. One row per signed-in browser, holding the refresh token.
autonumber
actor U as User
participant APP as Web App
participant API as Backend API
participant IDP as Identity Provider
participant DB as Session Store
%% @section Ask the identity provider
%% @summary The browser is sent to the provider with a hash of a secret it will prove later.
%% @step The user chooses to sign in. The app has no session cookie yet, so it has to send them to the provider.
U->>APP: Click "Sign in with Acme"
%% @step A random verifier and state are made for this attempt only. The verifier proves later that whoever swaps the code is the one who started the login.
%% @payload.result sessionStorage["pkce"] = { "verifier": "dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk", "state": "7f3a" }

APP->>APP: Create PKCE verifier and state
save both in sessionStorage
%% @step The browser goes to the provider with only the hash of the verifier. Nothing secret travels in the URL.
%% @payload.query response_type=code&client_id=web&redirect_uri=https://app.example/callback&code_challenge=Qm9...&code_challenge_method=S256&state=7f3a

APP->>IDP: GET https://id.acme.example/authorize
code_challenge, state
%% @step The password is typed on the provider's page, so our app and backend never handle it.
IDP->>U: Login page
%% @step The provider checks the password and asks for a second factor if the account has one.
U->>IDP: Email, password, MFA code
%% @section Swap the code for tokens
%% @summary The backend, not the browser, redeems the code and ends up holding the tokens.
alt Login approved
%% @step The provider sends the browser back with a one-time code. The app checks that state matches what it saved, which blocks forged callbacks.
%% @payload.headers Location: https://app.example/callback?code=SplxlOBeZQ&state=7f3a

IDP-->>APP: 302 Found
Location: /callback?code=…&state=7f3a
%% @step The app hands the code and the original verifier to its own backend. Tokens will be issued to the backend, not the browser.
%% @payload.body { "code": "SplxlOBeZQ", "code_verifier": "dBjftJeZ4CVP-mB92K27uhbUJU1p1r_wW1gFWFOEjXk" }

APP->>API: POST /auth/callback
code, verifier
%% @step The backend redeems the code with its client secret. The provider rejects it if the verifier does not hash to the challenge from step 3.
%% @payload.headers Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
%% @payload.body grant_type=authorization_code&code=SplxlOBeZQ&code_verifier=dBjftJ…&client_id=web&client_secret=•••&redirect_uri=https://app.example/callback
%% @timeout 5 s, then the sign-in fails and the user can start again

API->>IDP: POST https://id.acme.example/token
code, verifier, client secret
alt Code and verifier accepted
%% @step The code is now used up. The provider answers with three tokens.
%% @payload.body { "id_token": "eyJhbGciOi…", "access_token": "eyJraWQiOi…", "refresh_token": "8xLOxBtZp8", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 600 }

IDP-->>API: 200 OK
id_token, access_token, refresh_token
%% @step The backend checks the id_token signature, issuer, audience and expiry before trusting who the user is.
API->>API: Verify id_token
%% @step A session row ties a random session id to the user and their refresh token, so the browser only ever holds the session id.
%% @payload.sql INSERT INTO sessions (sid, user_id, refresh_token, expires_at) VALUES ('s_3f9a…', 'u_9', '8xLOxBtZp8', '2026-11-28T10:00:00Z')
%% @state before no session row for this browser
%% @state after one row s_3f9a… for user u_9 with the refresh token

API->>DB: INSERT session
sid, user, refresh token, expires
%% @step The session id goes into an HttpOnly cookie that page scripts cannot read. The user is now signed in and gets their profile back.
%% @payload.headers Set-Cookie: sid=s_3f9a…; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/
%% @payload.body { "user": { "id": "u_9", "name": "Ana" } }
%% @effect Audit log entry "login" with user id and time

API-->>APP: 200 OK
Set-Cookie: sid (HttpOnly, Secure)
else Code expired, reused or verifier wrong
%% @step The provider refuses the swap with a 400. Nothing is stored, so a stolen or replayed code gets an attacker nothing.
%% @payload.body { "error": "invalid_grant", "error_description": "Authorization code is invalid or expired" }

IDP-->>API: 400 Bad Request
error: invalid_grant
%% @step The app is told the sign-in failed and can start again from step 1.
%% @payload.body { "error": "login_failed", "message": "Sign-in could not be completed. Please try again." }

API-->>APP: 401 Unauthorized
"Sign-in could not be completed."
end
else User cancels or login fails
%% @step The provider sends the browser back to the same callback URL with an error and no code.
%% @payload.headers Location: https://app.example/callback?error=access_denied&state=7f3a

IDP-->>APP: 302 Found
Location: /callback?error=access_denied
%% @step The app clears the saved verifier and state and offers to try again. Nothing was stored on the backend.
APP-->>U: "Sign-in cancelled"
end
%% @section Use and refresh the session
%% @summary Every call carries only the cookie; the backend renews tokens without the user noticing.
loop Every API call while signed in
%% @step The cookie travels with each request. The app never attaches tokens itself.
%% @payload.cookies sid=s_3f9a…

APP->>API: GET /me
Cookie: sid
%% @step The backend looks up the session to find the user and their tokens.
%% @payload.sql SELECT user_id, access_token, refresh_token, expires_at FROM sessions WHERE sid = 's_3f9a…'
API->>DB: SELECT session WHERE sid = 's_3f9a…'
%% @step The session row comes back with the user and the stored tokens.
DB-->>API: 1 row: user u_9, tokens, expiry
opt Access token expired
%% @step Access tokens live for minutes. The backend quietly gets a new one with the refresh token, and the user notices nothing.
%% @payload.body grant_type=refresh_token&refresh_token=8xLOxBtZp8&client_id=web&client_secret=•••
%% @retry once, after a network error; the provider accepts the same refresh token until it has been used

API->>IDP: POST https://id.acme.example/token
grant_type=refresh_token
%% @step The provider rotates the refresh token and returns a new pair. Each one works once, so a stolen copy is useless after the next refresh.
%% @payload.body { "access_token": "eyJraWQiOi…", "refresh_token": "Q2vR7c1kLm", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 600 }

IDP-->>API: 200 OK
new access_token, refresh_token
%% @step Both new tokens replace the old ones in the session row.
%% @payload.sql UPDATE sessions SET access_token = 'eyJraWQiOi…', refresh_token = 'Q2vR7c1kLm' WHERE sid = 's_3f9a…'
API->>DB: UPDATE session tokens
end
%% @step The request succeeds as the signed-in user, who gets their profile back.
%% @payload.body { "id": "u_9", "name": "Ana", "email": "ana@example.com" }

API-->>APP: 200 OK
user profile
end
